thesis: An Alaska AI front desk is only as good as the page of facts behind it. The vet line wins because it reads one row of a spreadsheet, and the line it must not cross is the answer nobody wrote down.
falsifiable_by: An Alaska business in the feature winning with a free, unscoped widget, or the vet line's value coming from the model's own knowledge instead of the on-call schedule it reads.
supporting_facts: c5 emergency vet service: one number at midnight, calm-voiced AI says who's on call
c6 Vick: the AI is just reading a spreadsheet, the difference between panic and immediate relief
c12 Machuca: accidental adoption, a free widget with no plan
c13 Machuca: if getting it wrong would cost you a customer permanently, keep a human in that loop
c4 Pangborn: about 5 to 10 percent of customers use the chatbot (his estimate)
fair_counterpoint: Both success stories are one vendor's (Web 907) clients and every figure is self-reported. Only about 5 to 10 percent of the guide's customers use the bot by his own estimate. The feature reports no count of wrong answers. A careful local vendor tests with awkward hyper-local questions (c10). Demanding audit numbers from a $150 to $300 a month tool is a big-company standard. The counter-scene gets its own beat at full strength, then c12 and c15-c18 answer it: the careful version isn't the common one, per the SBDC, and the winners kept humans.
second_movement: c6 lands after scary-good: the magic is a lookup. The wins and the human line are the same rule from two sides, since the trouble starts where nobody wrote the answer down (c16 no road to every town, c11 weather day, c9 confidently make up an answer).
valence: upbeat with a condition earned from the owners and experts in the feature, not manufactured
runner_ups: narrow on purpose (builder): same thesis, weaker picture
nobody measures wrong answers (skeptic): kept as the counter-scene's last line, not the thesis, since 'nobody anywhere' is unprovable
the spreadsheet is the product (explainer): merged into the thesis
cross_challenge: All three analysts converged. Challenges applied by synthesis: (1) skeptic's thesis was a list, not a claim, so folded into the counter-scene. (2) explainer's 'only 5 to 10 percent use it' reads as a mark against, so it is drawn at true scale as a side door, not a failure. (3) builder's 'narrow on purpose' overreaches because the article never says the vet agent is narrow, so the film says 'reads a spreadsheet' only. (4) no claim about what the setup fee buys.
closing_question: Which question would you never let a bot answer without a person checking first, and which one is just a spreadsheet?
